text:
Alex: Heads-up — we're designing the new GPU capacity dashboard for Hosted + Dedicated. Need input on exact metric names, labels, and cardinality tradeoffs (SM occupancy, GPU mem, queue depth). Can runtime/infra + obs weigh in?

Priya: We already emit per-device gauges from the runtime: `runtime_gpu_sm_occupancy` (0-100), `runtime_gpu_mem_used_bytes`, `runtime_inference_queue_depth`. Currently labels: `device_id`, `host`, `model_id`, `model_version`.

Jen: Ok — that's useful but `model_id` kills cardinality for Hosted (PLG). We should stop exporting `model_id` at scrape time or relabel it. Add `pool_type` (`hosted`/`dedicated`) and `pool_id` labels so dashboards can split.

Marco: +1 on pool labels. For dashboards we should surface recording rules that pre-aggregate per-pool and per-cluster. Example PromQL we can add as recording rules:```promql
# per-pool SM occupancy (avg)
record:pool:gpu_sm_occupancy:avg
expr: avg by (pool_id) (runtime_gpu_sm_occupancy{job="runtime"})

# per-pool queue depth P95
record:pool:inference_queue_depth:p95
expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(runtime_inference_queue_depth_bucket[5m])) by (le, pool_id))
```

Priya: Note: `runtime_gpu_sm_occupancy` comes from a per-SM sampler in the kernel shim. It's expensive to push at high cardinality (per-core). We currently sample every 30s. If we need sub-10s resolution for Hosted latency debugging, we should only enable high-res for a subset of hosts or provide an on-demand tracing mode.

Sam: Dashboard UX thoughts: show a cluster map heatmap (SM occupancy avg), a per-pool lane that toggles Hosted/Dedicated, and a top-10 hosts table by queue depth + memory pressure. Also a small panel showing model-level anomalies but default collapsed.

Jen: For Dedicated, customers pay for capacity so we need tighter accounting: per-tenant `pool_id`, `reservation_id`. Retain those metrics at 30d. For Hosted, retain aggregated pools at 90d but drop host-level after 7d to save cardinality/TSDB cost.

Alex: Good call. What's the risk if we keep `model_version` label vs `model_id`?

Priya: `model_version` is slightly better but still many distinct values (A/B rollouts). Recommend we only export `model_version` when traffic > 100 reqs/min OR export `model_version_top` with top 10 versions.

Marco: Ops: we'll create recording rules and derived metrics: `pool_gpu_mem_used_bytes_total` (gauge sum by pool), `pool_gpu_sm_occupancy_avg`. Then dashboards query those. Also recommend alert rules: `pool_gpu_sm_occupancy_avg > 90` for 5m and `pool_inference_queue_depth_p95 > 50` for 3m.

Jen: Implementation notes: infra will add relabel_config to drop `model_id` for Hosted in the scrape pipeline; runtime team to add `pool_id` tag on export; obs to own recording rules & dashboards.

Priya: We'll add `gpu_arch` label (e.g., A100/H100) and `cuda_major` — small cardinality so OK and useful for perf triage.

Sam: For the console UI, can we surface a per-pool historical capacity widget + recommended autoscale suggestions from Optimize? That needs the per-pool `max_capacity_gpus` metadata from infra.

Alex: Action items: create infra ticket + runtime PR + obs dashboard ticket. I opened redwood/infra#4321 summarizing this (link: https://redwood/infra/4321). Owners: Jen (infra) for relabels & retention, Priya (runtime) for tags & sampling, Marco (obs) for recording rules & dashboards, Sam (product/UI) for UX changes. Target: first pass in 2 weeks.

observability-bot: Created ticket OBS-980 to add recording rules and alerting (assigned to Marco).

Jen: I'll start the relabel patch — dropping `model_id` for hosted and adding `pool_id`. PR by EOD tomorrow.

Priya: I'll add `pool_id` to runtime exports and expose a `high_res` debug flag to flip sampling for a host set. PR WIP, ping me for testing.

Marco: I'll sketch the dashboards and post a wireframe in #design once recording rules are in. Will also add the PromQL examples to the ticket.

Alex: Great. If anyone has objections to the retention windows or alert thresholds, speak now. Otherwise I'll lock the tickets. :thumbsup:
